newsitem.title: BELGIUM: China will consider talks with Dalai Lama, MEP says.
newsitem.headline: China will consider talks with Dalai Lama, MEP says.

text.p: The Chinese authorities say they will consider the offer made by Tibet's spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, to renew talks on the country's future, an Italian Socialist MEP said on Tuesday.

"The Chinese said they were doubtful the Dalai Lama was sincere about putting aside the demand for Tibetan independence (from China), which was their only condition for restarting the dialogue, but they said they would be ready to start the dialogue if it was put aside," Luigi Colajanni told a news conference.
Colajanni made his comments in the European Parliament after a delegation of Socialist MEPs returned from their first visit to China and Tibet for many years.

"We will see in the coming weeks if the (Chinese) attitude corresponds to a genuine will," he said, after a week of talks in China and Tibet with the Chinese communist party, the government and European non-governmental organisations working in Tibet.

The Dalai Lama last month told the Parliament's foreign affairs committee he wanted to renew talks with Beijing, which collapsed in 1983, and was calling for autonomy, not independence for the Himalayan kingdom, invaded by China in 1959.
Colajanni said the delegation had also met Yulo Dawa Tsering, a Tibetan buddhist monk who had not been seen for months following his imprisonment by the Chinese.
Amnesty International and the Tibetan diaspora had voiced concerns about his safety.
The monk was now under house arrest but said conditions were better than prison, Colajanni said. REUTER
